given: a Property with rooms and a room let by the bed and a Staff Member reaching it with the front_desk capability
when: they open Rooms at that Property
then: every Unit at the Property comes back once, a bed under its room, with building, floor, type, capacity, status and the reason it was blocked
test_name: rooms.test.ts: rooms lists every unit at the property with its beds

given: the same Staff Member and a second Property they are not assigned to
when: they open Rooms at the second Property
then: nothing comes back, indistinguishable from a Property with no Units
test_name: rooms_and_beds.test.sql: whose Units they cannot read either

given: the Property's front_desk capability is disabled, the Organization's Subscription has lapsed (suspended or cancelled), or its front_office Entitlement is revoked
then: nothing comes back: the read carries all four commercial and reach gates in its own statement, the same way the booking form's Unit list does. That predicate is the only thing hiding the Units, because the table's select policy is reach alone
test_name: rooms.test.ts: rooms are absent when the capability is off; rooms.test.ts: rooms are absent when the subscription has lapsed; rooms.test.ts: rooms are absent when the entitlement is revoked

given: a Unit with an in-house Stay
then: the Unit is in house, with the Guest's name and the day they leave; the status column is not consulted for this because nothing writes occupied to it (the restrictive status policy's WITH CHECK falls through to false). The name is read through the Stay's Reservation, so a Stay with no Reservation, which is what a Resident's is, shows in house with no name
test_name: rooms.test.ts: an in house stay makes a unit occupied; rooms.test.ts: a stay with no reservation shows in house with no name; rooms.test.ts: nothing can write occupied to a unit

given: a Unit with a confirmed Reservation that covers tonight (starts_on <= the Property's today < ends_on, or no end), including an arrival not yet checked in; and a Unit whose next confirmed Reservation starts later
then: the first is reserved, with the day its Reservation starts; the second is free, with the arrival date of the earliest later Reservation shown beside it; a Reservation cancelled or with every night already gone is neither, and one checked in has its Stay in house, so its Unit is in house (RB-S1-04) and never reserved
test_name: rooms.test.ts: a unit is reserved tonight only by a confirmed reservation that covers tonight; rooms-view.test.tsx: says when the next arrival is beside a free room, and only for that room; rooms-view.test.tsx: has a word for reserved tonight and the next arrival in %s ×3

situation: A room let by the bed
given: a room let by the bed with three beds under it, and a room let by the bed that is out of order
then: the room is not sellable itself and carries no state of its own except out of order (ADR 0032), which covers every bed under it; otherwise each bed carries its own state, and the Property's counts count the beds, not the room
test_name: rooms.test.ts: a room with beds is counted by its beds

situation: TIME — tonight is the Property's day
given: a Property in a timezone where it is already tomorrow
then: in house and reserved are measured against app.property_today for that Property, not the server's calendar, and the map says which day it measured
test_name: rooms.test.ts: occupancy is measured against the property day

given: a Resident with a current Stay
when: they sign in to the Workspace
then: they reach nothing here: a Resident reaches their own Unit through their own Stay and no policy in this feature widens that (ADR 0009). Already proved by tests/database/resident_access_path.test.sql
test_name: resident_access_path

given: the map of RB-S1-01
then: rooms is the number of top-level Units and sellable the number of leaves; in house, reserved, free and blocked partition the leaves that are in service, a leaf out of order is counted apart, and the five add up to sellable. A free Unit's next arrival is information on the Unit, not a count
test_name: rooms.test.ts: the counts partition the sellable units; rooms-view.test.tsx: counts reserved tonight apart from free, and out of order apart from both

given: an active Organization and a Staff Member holding accommodation.configure at a Property they reach
when: they add 4 rooms from 301 on floor 3 in Block A, sleeping 2
then: four rooms 301 to 304 are written with that building and floor and an audit record naming the actor and the four; one statement writes the rooms, so a refused name writes none of them
test_name: rooms.test.ts: adding rooms writes them all; rooms.test.ts: a room name already at the property refuses the whole add; accommodation-audit.test.ts: adding, blocking and unblocking rooms each name the Property

given: same as RB-S2-01 with let by the bed on
then: two rooms and six beds: each room's beds are named A, B and C under it, each sleeps one, and the rooms are no longer sellable whole
test_name: rooms.test.ts: letting by the bed writes one bed per sleeping place

given: a Staff Member who reaches the Property but holds no role carrying accommodation.configure
then: refused (42501) before anything is written; the front desk role does not carry this permission
test_name: rooms_and_beds.test.sql: but cannot add one: the front desk role does not carry the permission

situation: Into a Property out of reach
given: a Staff Member holding the permission in Organization A
when: they add a room to a Property of Organization B
then: refused (42501), and a row naming Organization B with Organization A's Property is unrepresentable because of the composite key
test_name: rooms_and_beds.test.sql: and not to one of the same Organization they are not assigned to; rooms_and_beds.test.sql: a manager elsewhere cannot add a Unit to this Organization; rooms_and_beds.test.sql: a Unit naming one Organization and another's Property is unrepresentable

given: the Organization's Subscription is suspended or cancelled
then: refused (42501) by the commercial gate inside the insert policy. A past_due Subscription is a grace period and adds rooms as normal (OA-S1-14, ADR 0040)
test_name: a_lapsed_subscription_adds_no_unit

given: room 302 exists at the Property
then: the whole add is refused and nothing is written; the refusal names 302, which is the one thing a person can change. The partial unique index on (property_id, name) where parent_id is null is what refuses it
test_name: rooms.test.ts: a room name already at the property refuses the whole add; rooms_and_beds.test.sql: a room name already at the Property is refused by the index, not by a check

given: rooms 301 and 302 both let by the bed
then: each has a bed A: a bed's name is unique within its room, not within the Property. Proved by tests/database/unit_hierarchy.test.sql
test_name: unit_hierarchy.test.sql: two beds in one room cannot share a name

given: let by the bed on
when: they ask for a room sleeping 27
then: refused by the module: beds are named by letter and a room holds at most 26. The capacity constraint allows 64 for a room sold whole, which is a different thing. Numbering beds past Z is RB-S2-15
test_name: accommodation-add-units.test.ts: a room holds at most twenty six beds

given: the form
then: refused by the module; one to sixty in one go, so a typo does not create a hotel
test_name: accommodation-add-units.test.ts: an add is between one and sixty rooms

given: the insert grant
when: an insert names status, status_reason, id or created_at
then: refused (42501): the grant is a column list and those columns are not on it, so a Unit is born available with nothing to say
test_name: rooms_and_beds.test.sql: a Unit cannot be born blocked

situation: CONCURRENCY — two people add the same numbers
given: two Staff Members
when: both add 301 to 304 at the same moment
then: one succeeds and the other is refused by the unique index, exactly as in RB-S2-06; no application check took part
test_name: rooms.test.ts: two people adding the same numbers at once leave one add and one refusal

situation: Only a room is let by the bed
given: the form
when: they ask for suites let by the bed
then: refused by the module, and refused again by accommodation_units_nesting_check for every role: only a room may be a parent (ADR 0025)
test_name: accommodation-add-units.test.ts: only a room is let by the bed; unit_hierarchy.test.sql: a bed cannot admit its parent is a bed; unit_hierarchy.test.sql: and cannot claim a bed is a room: the foreign key reads the parent's own type

given: a whole room that already exists
when: they want to add beds under it
then: not this feature: the bulk add creates a room and its beds together. The trigger that would guard it — a room somebody is in cannot be divided — already exists, so the later command is a form and not a rule

given: a Property whose rooms are named, not numbered (Deniz Suite, G01)
when: the desk adds one from the Workspace
then: not this feature: the form takes digits only, because the batch counts on from the first number, and there is no rename or delete, so a typo is permanent. A named add is one room at a time, and correcting a name is its own command

situation: A dormitory of more than twenty-six beds
given: a room let by the bed that sleeps 40
then: not this feature: beds are named A to Z, so 26 is the cap. The cap comes from the naming and not from the business; numbering beds 1 to N past Z is the way out

given: an empty bed, and a Staff Member holding accommodation.configure
when: they block it with the reason "mattress being replaced"
then: the bed is blocked with that reason on it, an audit record carries the reason, it leaves the booking form's Unit list, and it is drawn blocked on the map
test_name: rooms.test.ts: a blocked unit is drawn blocked and leaves the booking form; rooms_and_beds.test.sql: a manager blocks an empty room with a reason; accommodation-audit.test.ts: adding, blocking and unblocking rooms each name the Property

given: the same bed
when: they block it with no reason or one under three characters
then: refused (23514): a blocked Unit carries a reason and an available one carries none
test_name: rooms_and_beds.test.sql: a Unit cannot be blocked without a reason; rooms_and_beds.test.sql: and an available Unit carries no reason

given: a bed with an in-house Stay
then: refused (55000): the person in it is not going anywhere because of a status. The trigger reads every Stay, not the ones the caller's policies let through
test_name: a_unit_somebody_is_in_cannot_be_blocked

situation: A room let by the bed
given: a room with beds under it
then: refused (55000): the room is not sellable and its beds are what a block means; block the bed. Taking a whole room out of order is a maintenance request (ADR 0032), which covers every bed under it. Blocking every bed of a room in one command is RB-S3-14
test_name: rooms_and_beds.test.sql: a room let by the bed is blocked bed by bed; rooms.test.ts: only a room let by the bed is refused a block, whole

given: an empty bed with a confirmed Reservation arriving next week
then: allowed. The Reservation stands — nothing in the product can move it yet — and the room calendar will show the two together. What the block does is refuse the check-in (RB-S3-06)
test_name: rooms_and_beds.test.sql: a Unit with a booking arriving later can still be blocked

given: the bed of RB-S3-05 on the arrival day
when: the front desk checks the Guest in
then: refused (55000) by a trigger on stays: a Stay in house cannot begin on a blocked or out-of-service Unit, for every role. The Reservation stays arrivable and the desk sees the Unit is unavailable
test_name: rooms_and_beds.test.sql: a Stay in house cannot begin on a blocked Unit, for every role; rooms_and_beds.test.sql: nor on one out of service; rooms_and_beds.test.sql: and its Guest cannot be checked in while it is

situation: CONCURRENCY — block and check-in at once
given: the same bed
when: one person blocks it while another checks a Guest into it
then: one of the two is refused whichever commits first. The block's BEFORE UPDATE trigger runs with the Unit row locked, and the check-in's trigger takes a share lock on that row before reading its status, so neither reads a status the other is changing. Proved on two connections, each holding its transaction open while the other is started
test_name: rooms.test.ts: a block waits for a check-in that has not committed and then refuses; rooms.test.ts: a check-in waits for a block that has not committed and then refuses

given: a blocked bed
then: the bed is available with no reason on it, an audit record is written, and it is back on the booking form's Unit list
test_name: rooms_and_beds.test.sql: a manager unblocks it; rooms_and_beds.test.sql: and the reason goes with the block; accommodation-audit.test.ts: adding, blocking and unblocking rooms each name the Property; rooms.test.ts: an unblocked bed is back on the booking form, with no reason on it (RB-S3-08)

given: a Staff Member reaching the Property without accommodation.configure
then: refused: the update policy hides the row, so the update changes nothing (no error from the database), and the module answers that the Unit cannot be blocked or unblocked, which is the same answer as a Unit out of reach
test_name: rooms_and_beds.test.sql: nor block one: the update finds no row and the Unit is as it was; rooms.test.ts: blocking without the permission is answered as a unit that cannot be blocked

situation: A block is the only update
given: the update grant
when: an update names name, unit_type, capacity, building, floor, parent_id, property_id or organization_id
then: refused (42501): a policy bounds rows and a grant bounds columns, and the only columns a Staff Member may change on a Unit today are its status, the reason, and updated_at
test_name: rooms_and_beds.test.sql: a Unit cannot be renamed; rooms_and_beds.test.sql: nor grown; rooms_and_beds.test.sql: nor moved to another floor; rooms_and_beds.test.sql: nor a bed moved to another room; rooms_and_beds.test.sql: nor moved to another Property

given: a blocked Unit
then: nothing: a Unit has no rate and blocking one posts to no Folio and refuses nothing about money. Named so the absence is a decision

situation: REVERSAL — a room added by mistake
given: room 4O1 added with a letter O
then: it is blocked with a reason and stays: no DELETE grant exists on accommodation_units. Removing a Unit nothing has ever named is a later command and is drawn as an open question in use-case.mmd
test_name: a_unit_is_never_deleted

situation: A blocked Unit and the booking form
given: the bed of RB-S3-01
when: the front desk opens the booking form
then: the bed is not offered: listBookableUnits and createReservation exclude blocked alongside out_of_service, a blocked room hides its beds too, and a booking naming one anyway is refused with the module's one sentence for every reason, "that booking cannot be taken"
test_name: rooms.test.ts: a blocked unit is not bookable; rooms.test.ts: a blocked room hides the beds under it

given: a room with twelve free beds that is to be renovated
when: the desk wants them all blocked with one reason
then: not this feature: it takes twelve blocks today. Blocking every free bed of a room in one command, with one reason, is a loop in the module over the rule the database already keeps. Taking the whole room out of order for a repair is a maintenance request (ADR 0032)

given: a room added with a mistyped name, the wrong type or the wrong capacity, that no Reservation or Stay names yet
when: the desk wants to correct it
then: not this feature: a Unit's update grant is its status, the reason and updated_at (RB-S3-10), and there is no rename or delete, so such a mistake cannot be corrected today. The way out is an edit command for name, type and capacity that refuses once anything names the Unit
